scenes.heading: Blameless Postmortems
scenes.narration: A blameless postmortem turns a painful incident into durable organizational learning by focusing on systems instead of scapegoats.

scenes.heading: Why blameless matters
bullets: People report honestly when they aren't punished
Failures usually stem from systems, not individuals
Fear hides the real contributing factors
scenes.narration: When engineers know they will not be punished, they report what actually happened instead of a sanitized version. Most failures trace back to weak systems and missing guardrails rather than one careless person. Fear of blame hides the very contributing factors you need to see, so psychological safety directly produces better fixes.

scenes.heading: The postmortem process
scenes.narration: You begin by reconstructing an objective timeline from logs and the scribe's notes. Then you ask why repeatedly to move past the surface symptom toward the systemic causes. You capture the contributing factors, assign action items with clear owners and dates, and share the writeup widely so the whole organization learns.

scenes.heading: Blameless vs blameful
scenes.narration: A blameful culture asks who caused the outage, which drives information underground and lets the same incident recur. A blameless culture asks what conditions allowed the failure to happen at all. That shift keeps information flowing and turns each incident into a lasting systemic improvement.

scenes.text: The goal isn't to find who to blame — it's to find what to change so the next person can't make the same mistake.
scenes.narration: The goal of a postmortem is never to find someone to blame, but to find what to change so the next person cannot fall into the same trap.
